text:
ashwin: Heads-up — cluster-autoscaler just drained a GPU node in us-west-2 that still had 2 model-serving pods in Running state. Pods had PDBs so they bounced to other nodes but one got stuck Pending for ~3m, causing a small outage for latency-sensitive demo traffic.

maria: Ugh. Which node pool and priorityClass?

ashwin: gpu-pool-preemptible-2, priorityClass on the pods is 'gpu-batch' (low). The stuck pod is a stateful sidecar that writes to an ephemeral dir and didn't get deleted quickly.

kai: Can you paste the drain command that CA used or logs from autoscale-bot?

autoscale-bot: scaleDown: node "gwp-12" selectedfor scale-down; reason: underutilized; emptyAfter: 600s; drainCommand: "kubectl drain gwp-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --pod-selector='!critical=true'"

jess: I hate that --delete-local-data. For GPUs we usually prefer graceful eviction so model servers can flush KV caches. Maybe we need a preDrain hook.

ashwin: Agreed. Ideas we floated: add an annotation like "inference.redwood.com/pre-drain-hook=true" and a controller that POSTs /_flush to pods before the drain proceeds. For now we can tune CA to respect a node annotation to skip scale-down when it has tipsy pods.

tom: Also, PDBs are doing what they should — they prevented deletion until a replica could be scheduled. But because we have tight GPU capacity in the AZ, scheduling failed. Two levers: loosen PDB (maxUnavailable: 1) for non-production, or make pods more preemptible by using lower priorityClass/taints/tolerations so they get evicted earlier and rescheduled to cheaper nodes.

maria: Don't want to relax PDB for prod chatbots. Maybe set a separate priorityClass 'gpu-critical' (value 1000000) for latency-critical and 'gpu-preemptible' for background batches. Also we can set PodSpec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds to >= 30s and add lifecycle preStop to start flush.

kai: Quick config snippet that helped us in staging (shared here):
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: model-serving-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: model-serving
```
Use minAvailable instead of maxUnavailable for critical services.
```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: gpu-critical
value: 1000000
globalDefault: false
description: "Critical inference traffic"
```

jess: Also ensure the nodePools have different autoscaler configs. For gpu-pool-preemptible-2 set scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 15m and scaleDownUnneededTime: 20m so we don't kill nodes right after burst adds.

ashwin: Noted. Two immediate ops items: (1) add preStop hook and terminationGracePeriodSeconds to model-serving chart; (2) create a small controller that annotates nodes with "inference.redwood.com/scale-down-blocker=true" while graceful shutdown is running, and autoscale-bot will skip those (we can update CA to check API?).

maria: For (2) we could also annotate the pod with "disruption.protected=true" and have a mutating admission add a finalizer until flush completes. Finalizers are safer than node annotations.

kai: CA doesn't know about pod finalizers — but kube will refuse to delete pods with finalizers until controller removes them, which gives time. Works well.

tom: Cost note: keeping nodes warm increases cost. We should only use long-lived blockers for high-value production routes. For background workloads set lower priority and no PDB. Estimated extra cost if we increase scaleDownDelayAfterAdd to 15m: ~3-4% on that pool during steady-state.

ashwin: Ops playbook I'm thinking:
1) tag critical deployments with priorityClass=gpu-critical and add preStop flush and terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
2) background jobs -> priorityClass=gpu-preemptible, no PDB, tolerate preemptible TAINT:preemptible=true
3) add mutating webhook to inject finalizer/flusher for critical pods
4) tweak cluster-autoscaler settings on gpu pools: scaleDownDelayAfterAdd=15m, scaleDownUnneededTime=20m, includeExtraNodeGroups: false
5) run canary for 24h in staging us-west-2

jess: +1. Also add an alert: if >2 pods hit Pending due to GPU scheduling after a scale-down, page oncall. 

maria: I'll open a PR with podSpec changes and the webhook skeleton. Ashwin, can you update the autoscaler config and add the small check in autoscale-bot to skip nodes with label "inference.redwood.com/scale-down-blocker=true"?

ashwin: Yep, I'll push a patch to autoscale-bot and schedule a CA config rollout tomorrow morning.

sre-bot: deploy status: autoscale-bot patch queued in canary; CA config staged to gpu-pool-preemptible-2.

kai: Thanks. After rollout let's run a synthetic load to validate no more stuck pods on drain. Also record the incident in postmortems/ with the steps.

tom: small follow-up: consider adding a node-level eviction annotation TTL so if a controller accidentally leaves a blocker we don't leak forever. e.g., infer.blocker.expiry=2026-04-01T12:00:00Z

jess: Good call. Ok moving this to RTM: PRs from maria and ashwin; poi: staging test 24h; alert rule; postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:"
